terms: Computational graph and circuit: nodes are attention heads or feedforward neurons, edges are flows through the residual stream, and a circuit is the subgraph responsible for task performance (Preliminaries and Definitions).

Functional node: actively transforms its input, producing output whose representation or semantics differs substantially. Passthrough node: relocates input features downstream with minimal modification (Preliminaries and Definitions).

Masking coefficients c_n = {c_{n,u}, c_{n,p}, c_{n,f}}: probabilities that a node is unimportant, passthrough, or functional, summing to 1. A node is a candidate if c_p + c_f > c_u. Masks are soft in training and hard via argmax at evaluation (S³martCirc Overview).
Sim(A) = ÂÂ^T ⊙ (11^T − I): pairwise cosine similarity between token rows, excluding self-similarity (Important Node Classification).
FI(X,Y) = ||Sim(X) − Sim(Y)||_F / ||Sim(X)||_F: normalized change in token-similarity structure from a node's input to its output (Important Node Classification).
L_disc = α·KL(P_orig || P_mask) − (1−α)·log P_mask(y) (Important Node Discovery).
L_class = Σ over important nodes of [−c_f·FI − c_p/FI], which rewards high FI for functional nodes and low FI for passthrough nodes (Important Node Classification).
L_sparsity: three terms, for confidence (push coefficients to binary values), validity (coefficients sum to 1), and sparsity (penalize c_p + c_f) (S³martCirc Training Process).

Evaluation metrics: Circuit Size is the number of nodes in the end-to-end connected circuit. Acc. is the percent accuracy drop when the circuit nodes are masked. Logit. is the change in logit for the original prediction (Experiment Setup).
